statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 5% in the low band during the final hour of the CME weekend halt.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged over the 22:00-00:00 UTC Globex reopen, where thin Sunday liquidity and already-published weekend Hormuz rhetoric can produce a gap and two-way repricing. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: CME weekend halt holds Tail at 5% into the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen; Sunday Hormuz rhetoric and a 5% 10-year keep Stress moderate at 33%
body: This assessment is made in the final hour of the CME weekend halt, so no live NQ price path is observable and none is asserted. The standing references are Friday's NQZ26 settle at 29,917.25 (+0.59%, session range 29,648.00-29,993.25) and NDX cash at 29,644.17 (+0.67%), which closed near the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range on a triple-witching expiry that Bloomberg reports covered roughly $7 trillion of US options notional, the second largest on record. That close is therefore partly mechanical rather than clean directional evidence. VIX ended at 14.81 (-4.08%), near the low of its 14.80-15.63 range. The macro backdrop is restrictive: the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75%-4% on 17 September in a 12-0 vote, with 16 of 19 dots pointing to at least one further hike this year. The 10-year was around 5.006% on Friday against H.15 observations of 4.94% on 17 September, and the 2-year near 4.75%. Cross-asset evidence is conflicting rather than aligned: WTI settled at $100.30 (-1.58%) and Brent at $103.87 (-0.91%), both lower for a third session as Saudi ship-to-ship workarounds moved 2.8m bpd through Hormuz over six days, while equities rose and yields held near 5%. Friday's internals were similarly split, with semiconductor leadership against a 4-4 megacap tape and negative communication services. Conflict of this kind supports moderate Stress rather than elevated Tail. The live geopolitical input is Sunday rhetoric rather than a new kinetic discontinuity: Iran's parliament speaker said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until Tehran's conditions are met and that Iran's hand is on the lever, and Iranian lawmakers raised the prospect of a nuclear policy shift, with the foreign minister travelling to the UN General Assembly. That is a genuine gap catalyst into the 22:00 UTC reopen, which is why the danger window covers the first two hours of Globex trade, but it is not observed one-way price structure. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read and found stale and partial for this run: it was collected at 19:05 UTC with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was used only as latest-session confirmation of Friday's split internals and not as price-path evidence. Tail is accordingly held at the cycle floor, with no amplifier observed while the venue is shut.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe a stable low-Tail regime. Tail held between 4% and 5% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress drifted from 24% late on 19 September to a 30-33% band through the Sunday hours as the post-hike rate backdrop and the elevated oil complex accumulated. Confidence ranged from 70% to 76%, easing late in the window as the weekend halt lengthened the distance from the last live price path. Dominant mode was normal in every hour, consistent with a closed venue and no observable structure.
outlookSummary: The cycle spans the final hour of the CME weekend halt, the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, the Asian and European sessions, and the Monday US cash session through the 20:00 UTC close. Tail is projected to stay inside the low band in all 24 hours, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON throughout. The projected peaks are 11% at the 13:00 UTC hour containing the US cash open, 10% in the hour after it, and 9% at both the Globex reopen and the power hour into the close. The reopen is scored as the narrow danger window because thin Sunday liquidity meets already-published weekend Hormuz rhetoric. Monday's scheduled calendar is light - Fed Goolsbee at 10:30 UTC and the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC - with the denser slate of Richmond Fed, Fed speakers, note auctions and flash PMIs arriving from Tuesday. Every projected level is conditional risk: no future price structure is treated as already observed, and the scores would be revised on the observed path at each hourly assessment.

Tail is set near the cycle floor on that conditional basis, not on any observed structure.
